In this review, we critically evaluate the epigenetic, transcriptional, post-transcriptional, translational, and post-translational mechanisms through which lncRNAs regulate PD-associated pathways, either directly or via miRNAs. Furthermore, we have systematically evaluated individual lncRNAs implicated in in vitro and in vivo PD models, with an emphasis on the competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) activity of lncRNAs, their downstream molecular targets, and their contribution to dopaminergic neuron vulnerability. In conclusion, several lncRNAs emerge as promising modulators of pathways linked to key PD-associated genes, suggesting that ncRNA networks may shape the molecular architecture of PD. Overall, this review provides a comprehensive and critical evaluation of lncRNA regulation in PD, emphasising the need to shift from descriptive associations to mechanistic, disease-relevant validation of lncRNAs in familial PD and subsequent therapeutic evaluation.

title: Endothelial JMJD3 protects against hypertensive vascular injury by interacting with FOXM1 to activate PHGDH transcription.
abstract: Endothelial dysfunction, driven by oxidative stress, is a hallmark of hypertensive vascular injury. Histone demethylase Jumonji domain-containing protein 3 (JMJD3) is considered as a pivotal regulator in cardiovascular biology. However, its role in governing endothelial redox homeostasis and mitochondrial integrity during hypertensive vascular injury remains largely unexplored. Hypertensive model was induced in mice via AngiotensinⅡ (AngII) infusion. Recombinant adeno-associated virus serotype 9 (AAV9) carrying JMJD3, phosphoglycerate dehydrogenase (PHGDH) or shPHGDH under the control of endothelial-specific Tie2 promoter was administered 4 weeks before Ang II infusion. Ang II-incubated human aortic endothelial cells (HAECs) were used to model hypertension-associated endothelial injury in vitro. The molecular mechanism was explored by using CUT&Tag sequencing, RNA sequencing, immunoprecipitation and mass spectrometry analysis and chromatin immunoprecipitation quantitative polymerase chain reaction (ChIP-qPCR) assay. JMJD3 expression was reduced, accompanied by increased levels of the repressive histone mark H3 lysine 27 trimethylation (H3K27me3) in aortas from hypertensive individuals and Ang II-infused mice as well as in Ang II-treated HAECs. Endothelial JMJD3 overexpression lowered blood pressure and attenuated vascular injury in Ang II-induced hypertensive mice. In HAECs, JMJD3 overexpression improved endothelial function, preserved mitochondrial function, and reduced mitochondrial ROS accumulation, whereas JMJD3 silencing or pharmacological inhibition exacerbated endothelial and mitochondrial dysfunction. Mechanistic studies revealed that forkhead box protein M1 (FOXM1) interacted with and stabilized JMJD3, facilitating its recruitment to the PHGDH promoter to activate PHGDH transcription. Endothelial PHGDH-mediated serine synthesis contributed to the maintenance of vascular homeostasis in Ang II-induced hypertensive mice, with its protective role further supported by PHGDH loss- and gain-of-function experiments in Ang II-treated HAECs. Notably, PHGDH deficiency largely attenuated the protective effects of endothelial JMJD3 overexpression in both hypertensive mice and Ang II-treated HAECs. Our findings demonstrate that endothelial FOXM1-JMJD3-PHGDH axis plays a protective role in hypertensive vascular injury. Preventive modulation of this epigenetic-metabolic signaling axis may represent a potential strategy for preventing hypertensive vascular injury.

title: Exposure-oriented molecular profiling and machine learning prioritize the citrus flavonoid nobiletin as an antitumor candidate for colorectal cancer: integrated pharmacological evaluation.
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major health burden, and the pharmacologically relevant constituents of complex natural-product preparations are difficult to prioritize because chemical presence does not necessarily reflect systemic exposure. Here, we established an exposure-oriented pharmacological workflow integrating ultra-performance liquid chromatography-quadrupole time-of-flight tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-QTOF-MS/MS) serum profiling, machine learning, public human CRC single-cell RNA sequencing, target integration, molecular modeling, and experimental evaluation to identify and characterize a prioritized bioactive candidate from Wumen Xianzhu Jiedu Decoction (WMXZJDD). Serum profiling after oral administration annotated 127 serum-exposure-related features, including 42 prototype components and 85 putative metabolites. After parent-compound mapping, deduplication, and structural filtering, 47 exposure-related parent compounds were retained for machine-learning prioritization. Nobiletin (NOB), a citrus-derived polymethoxylated flavonoid, ranked first according to the four-model composite prioritization score (0.77). Integrative analyses supported MAPK/JNK signaling as a candidate mechanism underlying NOB activity. NOB inhibited CT26 cell proliferation (24-h IC50, 70.8 μM) and reduced EdU incorporation, accompanied by increased JNK phosphorylation and upregulation of Beclin-1, ATG5, and NCOA4. In syngeneic CT26 tumor-bearing mice, NOB suppressed tumor growth without treatment-associated body-weight loss. These findings prioritize NOB as an anti-CRC candidate within an exposure-informed screening framework and illustrate the potential of integrating serum profiling, machine learning, and pharmacological evaluation for active-component discovery from complex natural-product preparations.

title: p53 supports healthy aging.
abstract: p53 is a master regulator of cellular stress responses that is also implicated in the aging process. Its role in aging is often considered an example of antagonistic pleiotropy (AP), where it acts beneficially as a tumor suppressor early in life, but detrimentally in late life, for example by driving accumulation of stress-associated, pro-inflammatory senescent cells. However, the causal role of p53 in aging is not well-defined, and the AP model has not been definitively tested through loss-of-function studies. Here we show, contrary to the prediction of AP, that p53 promotes healthy aging in mouse liver by suppressing excessive inflammation and maintaining metabolic function. Multimodal RNA, protein, epigenetic and spatial profiling at the single-cell level in aged mouse liver confirmed age-dependent increase in p53 pathway activation. Hepatocyte-specific knockout of p53 in livers of aged mice, but not of young mice, increased inflammation and immune infiltration. Mechanistically, p53 suppressed DNA replication stress and DNA damage, known precursors to inflammatory signaling. In aged hepatocytes, p53 also directly targeted and maintained expression of metabolic genes, and knockout of p53 sensitized aged mice to metabolic stress-induced liver damage. Complementing these loss-of-function data, pharmacological activation of p53 with the small-molecule MDM2 inhibitor HDM201 in aged mice reversed age-associated suppression of metabolic genes, decreased age-associated inflammation and delayed onset of frailty. These results identify p53 activity in aged tissue as protective rather than degenerative. Importantly, this protective function is pharmacologically targetable, potentially for the benefit of healthy aging in humans.

title: Stage-Dependent Requirement for SETX in Human Motor Neuron Maturation and Survival.
abstract: Senataxin (SETX) is an RNA/DNA helicase involved in transcription, RNA processing, R-loop resolution, and genome maintenance. Mutations in SETX cause neurological disorders, but its role in human motor neuron (MN) development remains unclear. Here, we examined SETX function using isogenic SETX knockout (KO) human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs), shRNA-mediated knockdown, and direct conversion of fibroblasts into MNs. SETX expression increased during differentiation from hiPSCs to neural progenitor cells (NPCs) and MNs. SETX loss slowed hiPSC and NPC proliferation without preventing MN generation. However, SETX-deficient MNs developed shorter neurites, dystrophic swellings, and progressive neuronal loss. MEA recordings showed reduced firing and burst activity and almost no synchronized network bursts. RNA hybrid accumulation increased after SETX loss, with the largest relative increase in MNs among the cell types examined. RNA-seq revealed altered neurodevelopmental gene expression at the NPC stage and during MN differentiation, together with increased expression of stress- and apoptosis-associated genes. Proteomic analysis identified changes in proteins involved in neuronal structure, synaptic function, RNA regulation, and cellular homeostasis. Concordant decreases in selected RNAs and proteins supported disruption of neuronal structural and synaptic programs. Together, these findings reveal a stage-dependent requirement for SETX and identify SETX as an important regulator of transcriptional programs governing human MN maturation, function, and survival, providing a mechanistic framework for understanding the selective MN vulnerability associated with SETX-linked neurological diseases.

title: Methamphetamine use reshapes cellular and plasma immune signatures in a lineage-specific manner in people with HIV.
abstract: Methamphetamine use is common among people with HIV (PWH) and is associated with worse neurocognitive and clinical outcomes, but how it reshapes HIV-associated immune dysregulation across cell types and compartments is unknown. In this cross-sectional and observational study, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from controls without HIV, PWH without methamphetamine use and PWH who use methamphetamine, then scored pathway enrichment, cytokine response and transcription factor activity in each cell population. We then profiled plasma from the same three groups in a larger set of participants by targeted proteomics, with PWH who use cocaine added as a stimulant comparison. In the single-cell data, methamphetamine use acted in opposite directions across lineages. HIV-associated changes were reversed most often in monocytes and CD8 + T cells, with interferon, antigen presentation and JAK-STAT programs shifting in monocytes and IFN-γ, IL-2 and MYC programs shifting in CD8 + T cells, whereas HIV-associated proliferative and TNF signaling programs persisted in CD4 + and γδ T cells of Meth+HIV participants. Central memory CD8 + T cells of Meth+HIV participants showed reduced type 1 effector programs. In plasma, HIV was associated with a cytotoxic lymphocyte activation signature (KLRK1, IFN-γ, TNF, granzyme B and CXCL9) that was further elevated with methamphetamine use, together with higher IL-6, CXCL13 and neurofilament heavy chain. IFN-γ was the most connected protein in the plasma interaction network, linking a cytotoxic module to a lymphoid chemokine module. These data define lineage- and compartment-specific immune consequences of methamphetamine use in PWH and nominate IFN-γ signaling, acting through monocyte antigen presentation and CD8 + T cell effector programs, together with TNF, IL-6 and CXCL13, as candidate mediators of neuroimmune dysfunction in PWH who use methamphetamine. Paired single-cell PBMC and NULISA proteomic profiling in PWH who use methHIV-linked T cell activation persists with meth, while monocyte IFN programs flip Meth reshapes CD8 + T cell interferon and effector programs in people with HIV Plasma cytotoxic and neuronal injury markers rise further with meth useMonocyte antigen presentation programs suppressed in HIV rebound with meth use.

title: Myeloid mDIC Deficiency Remodels Adipose Macrophages to an Efferocytosis-Associated State and Improves Metabolic Homeostasis During Obesity.
abstract: Obesity-associated adipose inflammation contributes to metabolic dysfunction, yet the mechanisms linking mitochondrial metabolism to macrophage efferocytosis remain incompletely understood. The mitochondrial dicarboxylate carrier (mDIC), encoded by SLC25A10 , regulates adipocyte function, but its role in macrophages remains unclear. Here, we investigated how myeloid mDIC deficiency affects mitochondrial function, macrophage heterogeneity, and metabolic homeostasis during diet-induced obesity. We observed reduced mDIC protein expression in subcutaneous white adipose tissue from individuals with obesity, whereas palmitate increased mDIC expression in mouse and human macrophages. Myeloid mDIC deletion preserved mitochondrial respiration under palmitate stress. Single-cell RNA sequencing of adipose stromal vascular cells from high-fat diet (HFD)-fed mice revealed an expanded efferocytosis-associated macrophage population and reduced proportions of inflammatory and lipid-associated macrophages. Consistently, mDIC-deficient macrophages exhibited increased Mertk expression and greater association with apoptotic cells. Pharmacological inhibition of mitochondrial ATP synthase or electron transport markedly suppressed apoptotic cell uptake, including the quenching-resistant fraction, without substantially affecting macrophage viability. In vivo , myeloid mDIC deletion attenuated HFD-induced weight gain, improved insulin sensitivity, and increased CD11c⁻CD206⁺ adipose macrophage abundance, accompanied by elevated expression of alternative activation-associated markers. Together, these findings identify myeloid mDIC as an important regulator of macrophage mitochondrial function and adipose immune remodeling during obesity, suggesting a novel mechanism by which mitochondrial bioenergetics contribute to macrophage apoptotic-cell handling and metabolic homeostasis.

title: IL-15 superagonist induces robust STAT5 phosphorylation to support the differentiation and survival of tumor-relevant memory precursor effector-like CD8 T cells, enhancing long-term antitumor protection.
abstract: Common gamma chain cytokines drive CD8 T cells to proliferate and acquire effector function, but strong interleukin-2 (IL-2) signaling also drives terminal differentiation at the expense of memory. Engineered cytokine agonists are now entering the clinic, yet which property of cytokine signaling determines whether an expanding effector retains memory potential and the role of memory in long term responses remains unresolved. We use a resectable, spontaneously metastatic mouse model of lung adenocarcinoma to compare an IL-15 superagonist with PD-1 blockade, alone and in combination, and to follow tumor-relevant CD8 T-cell clones from treatment through surgery to metastatic relapse. We combine flow cytometry with paired single-cell RNA and T-cell receptor sequencing of tumor, tumor-draining and non-draining lymph nodes. We use receptor blockade and phosphorylation flow cytometry in OT-1 cultures to define the signaling requirement, and subset depletion with tumor rechallenge to test the resulting memory. The IL-15 superagonist expands a cytotoxic CD8 T-cell state that retains IL-7Rα and lacks KLRG1, which we term memory-precursor effector-like (Tmpe). This state requires CD122 and accompanies STAT5 phosphorylation exceeding that induced by conventional IL-15 or IL-2, with minimal STAT3 engagement. Tumor-matched clonal diversity increases within a progenitor-like compartment of the tumor-draining lymph node, and the clones carrying this program are those recovered in non-draining lymph nodes long after tumor resection. Combination with PD-1 blockade reduces metastatic recurrence and extends survival. Unexpectedly, depletion of either CD4 or CD8 T cells alone fails to abrogate protection on rechallenge and only combined depletion does, unlike the memory established by PD-1 blockade, where loss of either subset is sufficient. Our data link the Tmpe state to CD122-dependent signaling accompanied by strong STAT5 and minimal STAT3 phosphorylation, and show that the clones carrying this state are those that persist in lymphoid tissue and protect against recurrence. This suggests that how an engineered cytokine engages STAT proteins, and not only how strongly, shapes whether an expanding effector retains memory potential, which is a testable design parameter for the next generation of cytokine agonists. What is already known on this topic: Strong γc cytokine signaling, exemplified by IL-2, drives CD8 T cells toward terminal effector differentiation at the expense of memory, and engineered cytokine agonists have entered the clinic without a defined principle for which signaling property should be optimized.What this study adds: An IL-15 superagonist that drives strong STAT5 phosphorylation with minimal STAT3 engagement generates a CD122-dependent cytotoxic CD8 T cell state that retains IL-7Rα, with associated persistence in lymphoid tissue after tumor resection and protect against metastatic recurrence. This memory is functionally distinct, since either CD4 or CD8 T cells alone are sufficient for protection on rechallenge, unlike the memory established by PD-1 blockade.How this study might affect research, practice or policy: These findings indicate that how an engineered cytokine engages STAT proteins as a design parameter for durable antitumor immunity, and that the durability of a cytokine agonist is best assessed in models permitting clonal tracking through resection into relapse.

title: SH2 Domain Protein E sustains perivascular fibroblasts to maintain arterial stability.
abstract: Developing arteries must withstand pulsatile blood flow while remaining sufficiently flexible to accommodate changing hemodynamic demands. Endothelial interactions with perivascular cells and the extracellular matrix (ECM) are essential for this balance, but the signaling mechanisms that coordinate them remain incompletely understood. We previously showed that SH2 domain protein E (She), an endothelial adaptor protein implicated in ABL signaling, is required to maintain the size and structural stability of the dorsal aorta (DA) in zebrafish embryos. she mutant embryos develop DA collapse and circulatory failure at 4-5 days post-fertilization, yet the underlying cause has not been identified. Here, we investigated the role of She in recruiting ECM-producing perivascular stromal cells to regulate the structural stability of the DA. She mutants had fewer collagen-producing perivascular stromal cells between the DA and posterior cardinal vein. This correlated with smaller perivascular col1a1 and col5a1 expression domains, reduced col1a1 transcript and Collagen I pro-peptide levels, and increased DA distensibility. Single-cell RNA sequencing independently identified a reduced relative abundance of a perivascular fibroblast subpopulation. In contrast, DA-associated mural cell number, laminin immunoreactivity, and local col4a1 transcript levels were not detectably altered. Partial ablation of mural cells alleviated DA narrowing and circulatory failure, while the nitric oxide donor sodium nitroprusside provided partial rescue. These findings support a contribution of mural cell-dependent vascular tone to the collapse of the mechanically vulnerable DA. Mutants also exhibited cardiac chamber enlargement, increased atrial and bulbus arteriosus deformation, atrioventricular regurgitation, and increased Elastin B accumulation in the enlarged bulbus arteriosus. However, endocardial-specific She expression failed to rescue circulatory failure, supporting its requirement in the vascular endothelium. Together, these findings argue that She functions in the vascular endothelium to recruit and/or maintain perivascular stromal cells, which produce fibrillar collagens required for arterial stability. These results reveal a new mechanism by which signals from the vascular endothelium promote ECM support to maintain arterial vascular stability.

title: The long intergenic noncoding RNA NllincUK regulates fecundity in the brown planthopper (Nilaparvata lugens).
abstract: The brown planthopper, Nilaparvata lugens, is a major rice pest whose outbreaks are largely driven by its high reproductive capacity. However, the contribution of long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) to fecundity regulation remains poorly understood. Here, transcriptome-based lncRNA profiling was conducted using high- and low-fecundity genotype populations reared under different density conditions across generations. A total of 13 874 putative lncRNAs were identified, with long intergenic noncoding RNAs (lincRNAs) representing the predominant class. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis identified three lncRNA modules significantly associated with fecundity, and putative target genes of these modules were associated with several reproductive and metabolic pathways based on exploratory functional annotation. From a module positively correlated with fecundity, a 490 bp lincRNA, NllincUK, was selected for further characterization. The expression of NllincUK increased after adult emergence, was highly enriched in the ovary, and was mainly localized in the cytoplasm. RNA interference (RNAi) of NllincUK reduced female fecundity by 56.73%, accompanied by decreased Vg and VgR transcript levels and reduced Vg protein abundance. NllincUK knockdown also delayed ovarian development, reduced ovarian egg number, and altered egg morphology. Moreover, oviposition performance was impaired, as indicated by shorter and fewer oviposition marks and reduced egg deposition in rice stems. These findings indicate that NllincUK contributes to maintaining normal female fecundity in N. lugens and provide new insights into lncRNA-mediated regulation of insect reproduction.

title: Lipid Nanoparticles (LNPs) in Anticancer Drug Delivery: Biological Barriers and Clinical Translation Potential.
abstract: During the COVID-19 pandemic, lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-based messenger RNA (mRNA) vaccines have been widely deployed in clinical practice, demonstrating the clinical feasibility of this delivery platform. Although applications of LNPs in cancer treatment are advancing rapidly, barriers to clinical translation remain. Therefore, this review aims to summarize the major barriers and translational potential of LNP-based strategies in cancer treatment. We systematically searched PubMed/MEDLINE for relevant literature on LNP design, formulation, and applications in anticancer drug delivery published up to May 2026, including preclinical studies, clinical trials, and reviews. LNPs played pivotal roles in cancer treatment by delivering pharmaceutical ingredients, including chemotherapeutic and immunotherapeutic drugs. By encapsulating the anticancer medicines, LNPs facilitated drug delivery to tumor sites and protected the payloads from degradation in vivo. Major barriers include protein corona formation, inefficient endosomal escape, hepatic accumulation, formulation instability, immunogenicity and toxicity, and challenges in manufacturing consistency and cost control. Clinically, liposomal chemotherapeutics have achieved regulatory approval, whereas LNP-based nucleic acid therapies for cancer remain predominantly investigational. Moreover, structural modifications on the major components of LNPs helped address these limitations. The latest advancements of LNP designs and applications in the delivery of nucleic acids and chemotherapeutic drugs exhibited better biocompatibility and therapeutic efficacy with improved safety profiles. LNP-based therapies hold potential for clinical applications in cancer treatment. Future efforts should focus on improving targeting and endosomal escape, reducing toxicity, and enhancing stability and manufacturing quality while controlling costs. Artificial intelligence-assisted design and biodegradable materials may support these developments and facilitate clinical translation.

title: Anti-Ro52 autoantibodies modulate the transcriptomic effects of autoantibodies targeting intracellular autoantigens.
abstract: Ro52/TRIM21 is a cytoplasmic protein that binds intracellular antibodies and drives their proteasomal degradation. Autoantibodies targeting Ro52 frequently co-occur with myositis-specific autoantibodies, including anti-MDA5, and patients with both autoantibodies have greater disease severity and interstitial lung disease risk. We previously demonstrated that internalized anti-MDA5 autoantibodies promote interferon-stimulated gene expression in cultured myoblasts. Here, we investigated the interactions between anti-Ro52 and coexisting autoantibodies, including anti-MDA5. Primary human skeletal muscle myoblasts were electroporated with purified IgG from healthy controls or patients with anti-MDA5, anti-Mi-2, or anti-PM/Scl antibodies, combined with anti-Ro52-positive IgG from patients with myositis, Sjögren's disease, or systemic sclerosis. Affinity-purified anti-Ro52 was also used to validate findings obtained using total IgG. Cells underwent bulk RNA sequencing 24 hours after internalization. Co-internalization of anti-Ro52 with anti-MDA5 enhanced the anti-MDA5-induced type I interferon transcriptional response and expression of type II interferon-inducible genes compared with anti-MDA5 and control IgG. Increased expression of IFNB1 , ISG15 , MX1 , and the interferon-γ-inducible inflammatory chemokines CXCL9 and CXCL10 was observed across independent patient-derived antibody combinations, anti-Ro52 preparations from multiple autoimmune diseases, and affinity-purified anti-Ro52. Conversely, co-internalization of anti-Ro52 with anti-Mi-2 or anti-PM/Scl reduced expression of transcripts associated with these nuclear autoantibodies. These findings demonstrate that anti-Ro52 autoantibodies potentiate the activation of interferon pathways stimulated by the internalization of anti-MDA5 antibodies. We propose that in patients with anti-MDA5 autoantibodies, co-existing anti-Ro52 antibodies may exacerbate disease by inhibiting the proteasomal degradation of internalized anti-MDA5 antibodies and thereby enhancing the expression of interferon and interferon-stimulated genes.

title: RBM15::MKL1 uncouples SPOC-dependent m 6 A remodeling from WTAP recruitment.
abstract: The recurrent t(1;22) translocation associated with pediatric acute megakaryoblastic leukemia generates the RBM15::MKL1 (RM) fusion protein that retains the RNA-binding and SPOC domains of RBM15. RBM15 recruits the N 6 -methyladenosine (m 6 A) methyltransferase complex (MTC), of which WTAP is a key regulatory component. How RM engages this machinery and whether the SPOC domain is required for its leukemogenic activity remain unclear. Here, we investigated the molecular determinants of WTAP recruitment by RBM15 and RM and their contribution to RM-mediated disruption of megakaryocyte differentiation. Structure-guided mutagenesis identified a conserved basic surface within the isolated RBM15 SPOC domain that is required for WTAP association. Unexpectedly, disruption of this surface or complete SPOC deletion failed to abolish WTAP association with full-length RBM15 or RM, indicating that additional determinants mediate MTC recruitment. In human erythroleukemia cells, RM impaired TPA-induced megakaryocytic maturation, as assessed by differentiation markers, polyploidization, and morphology; this blockade persisted following SPOC disruption. However, transcriptomic analysis demonstrated that RM lacking the SPOC domain elicited an attenuated gene expression response compared with unmutated RM, including alterations in WNT/β-catenin-associated genes. m 6 A-enriched RNA profiling further revealed extensive remodeling of the m 6 A epitranscriptome by RM, while SPOC deletion shifted RM-associated m 6 A changes toward a more wild-type-like state. Together, these findings demonstrate that although the SPOC domain contributes to RM-mediated molecular regulation, it is dispensable for stable MTC association and maintenance of the differentiation blockade, revealing previously unrecognized redundancy in RBM15-mediated recruitment of the m 6 A machinery. All data generated in this study are included in this article and its supplementary information. RNA-seq and EpiPlex data have been deposited in the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) repository and are accessible with the accession number GSE349759. SPOC deletion shifts RM-associated m 6 A changes and gene expression toward a wild-type-like state without restoring megakaryocyte maturation. The RBM15 SPOC domain is dispensable for WTAP recruitment by full-length RBM15 and the leukemogenic RBM15::MKL1 (RM) fusion.

title: Mechanism of NAT10 in Promoting Malignant Progression and Glycolysis in Cervical Cancer Revealed by Bioinformatics Analysis.
abstract: Cervical cancer (CC) progression is closely associated with aberrant epigenetic regulation. Although N-acetyltransferase 10 (NAT10), a key regulator of N4-acetylcytidine (ac4C) modification, promotes CC progression, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. NAT10 expression profiles across cell subpopulations were characterized using single-cell RNA sequencing data from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) and validated by quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) and Western blot. Functional roles were assessed using 3-(4,5-dimethylthiazol-2-yl)-2,5-diphenyltetrazolium bromide (MTT), Transwell, tube formation, and apoptosis assays, alongside glucose consumption, lactate production, and adenosine triphosphate/adenosine diphosphate (ATP/ADP) ratio measurements. RNA immunoprecipitation (RIP), actinomycin D (ActD), dual-luciferase reporter, and chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) assays were employed to investigate mechanisms, alongside in vivo tumor xenograft models and immunohistochemistry (IHC) analysis. NAT10 was found to be highly expressed in CC (p < 0.05, p < 0.01, p < 0.001). NAT10 knockdown significantly inhibited CC cell proliferation, migration, and angiogenesis, induced apoptosis, and decreased glucose consumption, lactate production, and the ATP/ADP ratio (p < 0.05, p < 0.01, p < 0.001). Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) upon NAT10 knockdown were enriched in metabolic pathways. Mechanistically, cAMP response element-binding protein 1 (CREB1) activated NAT10 transcription, while NAT10 mediated ac4C modification of 6-phosphofructo-2-kinase/fructose-2,6-bisphosphatase 4 (PFKFB4) to promote malignant phenotypes and glycolysis in CC cells (p < 0.05, p < 0.01, p < 0.001). Furthermore, NAT10 regulated PFKFB4 expression to modulate in vivo tumor growth, weight, and Ki67 expression (p < 0.001). In conclusion, CREB1 targets and activates NAT10 transcription. Upregulated NAT10 catalyzes ac4C modification of PFKFB4, driving malignant progression and glycolysis in CC, highlighting its therapeutic potential.

title: Coagulation cofactor von Willebrand factor promotes vascular calcification in patients with chronic renal failure and in a vascular calcification model.
abstract: Vascular calcification and coagulation disorders are highly prevalent in patients with chronic renal failure (CRF); however, whether a causal relationship between these two exist is not clear. This study investigated the role of the coagulation factor von Willebrand factor (vWF) in the pathogenesis of vascular calcification in CRF. RNA sequencing was used to detect changes in gene expression involved in coagulation cascades in human umbilical vascular endothelial cells (HUVECs) treated with Na2HPO4 and NaH2PO4, reaching a final total phosphate concentration of 3 mM. A rat model of vascular calcification was generated by feeding rats a diet containing 0.5% adenine and 1.2% phosphorus. vWF expression in HUVECs was determined using RT-qPCR and Western blot analyses. Gain- and loss- of function approaches were used to examine the effect of vWF on HUVEC calcification. A segment of radial artery and plasma of CRF patients were collected to analyze calcification and gene expression. The correlation between circulating levels of vWF and bone morphogenetic protein 2 (BMP2) was examined. vWF expression increased in Pi-treated HUVECs, which coincided with increased BMP2 expression. Circulating levels of vWF and BMP2 were significantly higher in CRF patients and in the vascular calcification rat compared to the respective controls. We found a positive correlation of vWF and BMP2. vWF promoted Pi-induced HUVEC calcification, which was attenuated by treatment with Noggin, an inhibitor of BMP signaling. These findings suggest that vWF promotes Pi-induced HUVEC calcification and vascular calcification in CRF, at least in part, through the involvement of BMP signaling.

title: Integrative GWAS and RNA-seq analysis identifies carbohydrate metabolism genes associated with yield traits under low nitrogen.
abstract: Nitrogen use efficiency (NUE) is a key determinant of sustainable wheat production, yet its genetic basis remains incompletely understood under variable nitrogen supply. Grain yield and quality traits exhibit distinct responses to different nitrogen dosages, and the genetic loci and core genes governing low-nitrogen adaptability have not been systematically dissected via multi-omics integration. We evaluated 191 wheat accessions under four nitrogen application rates (N0, N150, N210, N270) across two environments and implemented an integrated framework combining multi-model GWAS, LD-based locus consolidation, RNA-seq, and WGCNA analyses to identify candidate genes. Phenotypic analysis revealed strong trait-specific nitrogen responses, with spike number (SN), grain number per spike (GNS), and plant height (PH) peaking at N210, while thousand grain weight (TGW) declined and grain protein content (GPC) increased with increasing nitrogen. Based on TGW, SN, and GNS, adaptability scores and low-nitrogen tolerance indices were constructed to classify genotypes into four performance groups, identifying 41 accessions (21.5%) with both high yield stability and strong low-nitrogen tolerance. GWAS of adaptability traits and nitrogen-response indices identified 85 significant QTLs supported across environments and models, including multiple co-localized multi-trait loci. Integrative analysis incorporating transcriptomics and co-expression networks prioritized TraesCS7A02G040900, encoding a sucrose synthase, as the most plausible candidate gene underlying a TGW-associated locus. This gene exhibited consistent expression divergence between low nitrogen-tolerant and sensitive groups under both N0 and N210 conditions, indicating genetically determined regulation of carbon partitioning. Our work validates the power of integrating adaptability indices and multi-omics data to unravel the genetic architecture of wheat NUE. Carbon partitioning metabolism is proven to be a critical pathway connecting nitrogen status and yield performance, with TraesCS7A02G040900 represents a promising correlative candidate gene requiring subsequent functional characterization. The germplasm and molecular targets identified here lay a solid foundation for breeding nitrogen-efficient wheat.

title: Longitudinal profiling of urinary extracellular vesicle RNA reveals physiological variability and stable reference genes in healthy individuals.
abstract: Urinary extracellular vesicles (uEVs) have emerged as promising non-invasive molecular carriers for biomarker discovery, yet the physiological variability and tissue-associated characteristics of uEV RNA cargo in healthy individuals remain poorly defined. This knowledge gap limits the interpretation, normalization, and clinical translation of uEV-based transcriptomic studies. Here, we performed a longitudinal RNA-sequencing analysis of uEVs from 12 healthy donors, of whom six contributed complete longitudinal sample sets, to establish a molecular reference framework for physiological uEV transcriptomes. We systematically characterized inter- and intra-individual variation in uEV RNA cargo and found substantial transcriptomic heterogeneity despite relatively stable extracellular vesicle secretion levels over time. A conserved set of highly expressed genes was significantly enriched in ribosomal function and oxidative phosphorylation, indicating their role in fundamental cellular maintenance. Importantly, we identified 12 protein-coding genes that showed consistently low expression variance both across individuals and within individuals over time. Cross-dataset analyses using independent external and pan-cancer datasets further supported their potential utility as candidate reference transcripts for uEV RNA studies. Computational tissue deconvolution inferred predominant kidney- and bladder-associated transcriptomic signatures, while cell-type enrichment analysis showed relatively high enrichment scores for smooth muscle cells and mesenchymal stem cells. Together, this study defines the physiological landscape of healthy uEV transcriptomes, delineates key sources of biological variation, and provides candidate reference transcripts and tissue-associated molecular profiles to support the standardization and translational application of uEV-based molecular biomarker research.

title: Targeting bromodomain plant homeodomain finger transcription factor reverses melanoma immune evasion via the p53/PD‑L1 axis: A study integrating machine learning identification and methapyrilene repurposing.
abstract: Primary non‑response and acquired resistance limit immunotherapy efficacy in melanoma. Tumor‑cell transcriptional programs influence immune‑checkpoint signaling and susceptibility to T cell‑mediated killing. The present study aimed to identify actionable tumor‑intrinsic regulators of immune escape and evaluate their therapeutic tractability. Transcriptomic data from four melanoma immunotherapy datasets were integrated for differential expression analysis. Candidate genes were selected using three machine learning (ML) approaches. Subsequently, eight ML models and the SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis were used to prioritize response‑associated features. Pathway enrichment analysis explored biological pathways associated with the top‑ranked candidate gene. Drug‑gene interaction analysis, molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations identified therapeutic candidates. Gene overexpression and knockdown models were established by plasmid and short hairpin RNA transfection, respectively. Colony‑formation, Transwell, western blotting, cellular thermal shift, drug affinity‑responsive target stability and T‑cell co‑culture assays were performed. Six feature genes were identified. Particularly, bromodomain plant homeodomain finger transcription factor (BPTF) ranked highest and was negatively associated with immune therapy response. BPTF‑high samples demonstrated negative enrichment of the p53 pathway. In vitro, BPTF overexpression notably promoted melanoma clonogenic growth and invasion, suppressed p53 signaling, increased mouse double minute 2 (MDM2) and programmed death‑ligand 1 (PD‑L1) expression, and impaired CD8+ T‑cell activation and cytotoxicity. BPTF knockdown produced reciprocal effects. Chromatin immunoprecipitation‑quantitative PCR and dual‑luciferase assays supported BPTF‑mediated repression of TP53 and activation of CD274. Methapyrilene demonstrated stable predicted binding to BPTF, increased BPTF thermal and proteolytic stability, and attenuated BPTF‑associated malignant and immune‑evasive phenotypes. The combination with PD‑L1 blockade enhanced tumor‑cell killing and T‑cell effector responses compared with either treatment alone. In conclusion, BPTF associates melanoma progression with immune escape through the p53/PD‑L1 axis. Methapyrilene interacts with BPTF and provides a lead scaffold for developing BPTF‑directed agents in combination with PD‑L1 blockade to overcome immunotherapy resistance in the future.

title: NLRP3 Inflammasome Activation Dynamics are Shaped by Age, HIV-infection and Co- morbid Conditions.
abstract: With the advent of effective antiretroviral therapy, increased rates of age-related diseases such as cardiovascular disease and diabetes have been observed in people living with HIV (PLH). Persistent immune activation in PLH and age-related chronic inflammation are hypothesized to be drivers for the development of such diseases. Dysregulated NLRP3 inflammasome activation has been implicated in aging-related pathologies, but the combined impact of HIV and aging on inflammasome regulation remains poorly defined. To investigate this interplay, we enrolled a total of 147 subjects stratified by HIV status (positive/negative) and age. We found that older adults with increased co-morbidities and aging PLH had increased inflammasome activation at baseline in monocytes compared to younger adults (demonstrated by elevated caspase-1 activation, elevated levels of IL-1β and IL-18), and a blunted response to microbial stimuli (LPS and LPS + ATP stimulation), with decreased production of IL-1β and IL-18. RNA-seq of purified monocytes revealed cohort-specific transcriptional programs associated with aging, HIV infection, and comorbidities both at baseline and with stimulation. The HIV-negative young cohort followed a predictable trajectory of inflammasome activation that was also mirrored in the transcriptional data of isolated monocytes where we saw an overall predictable increase in inflammasome gene expression. This coherence was lost in both older adults with higher comorbidity burden and aging PLH, who showed decoupling of RNA and protein with respect to inflammasome activation. Increased IFN signaling was noted at baseline in HIV-negative older adults and in aging PLH. With LPS stimulation, WGCNA analysis identified a gene module enriched for neuronal signaling and extracellular matrix remodeling that exhibited a stepwise increase in expression from HIV-negative young adults to subjects with increased age, HIV-infection, and greater comorbidity burden. HIV-positive older adults were noted to have downregulation of genes associated with TLR4 signaling. Collectively, our findings reveal that HIV, Aging and co-morbid conditions all reshape inflammasome dynamics-marked by baseline hyperactivation and blunted responsiveness to pathogenic stimuli.

title: 17β-Estradiol exerts subtle synaptic and transcriptional effects in human cerebral organoids.
abstract: 17β-Estradiol, a major form of oestrogen, has been shown to regulate synapse formation, structure, and synaptic protein expression in the rodent brain and primary neuronal cultures. Less is known about how 17β-estradiol influences early neurodevelopment in human neurons. Addressing this gap, we used XX and XY human pluripotent stem cell (PSC)-derived cerebral organoids as a model to study the effects of 17β-estradiol on synapse formation and gene expression. Organoids were cultured until 45-60 days in vitro (DIV), from which air-liquid interface cerebral organoid (ALI-CO) slices were generated and cultured until 80 DIV. At this stage synaptogenesis is underway, and we tested whether exposure to 17β-estradiol influenced synapse structure or protein expression. Immunohistochemistry, bulk and single-nuclei RNA-sequencing analyses revealed that ALI-CO slices were predominantly glutamatergic, with a dorsal forebrain identity. ALI-CO slices expressed the oestrogen receptor genes ESR1, ESR2, and GPER1, together with the androgen receptor at differing levels, with no consistent receptor expression sex differences. To identify pre- and post-synaptic compartments, we used instant structured illumination microscopy (iSIM) of immunostained organoid slices for pre-synaptic Bassoon, and the post-synaptic GluN1 NMDA receptor subunit. Synapses, defined as Bassoon-GluN1 overlaps, were abundant and morphologically diverse. Acute (24 h) 17β-estradiol exposure produced consistent but largely non-significant increases in synapse and puncta number and GluN1 puncta intensity and size, a significant reduction in GluN1 puncta solidity, and reduced variability between samples. These directional changes were reproduced across ALI-CO slices generated from four PSC-lines (two XX and two XY). By contrast, repeated exposure to 17β-estradiol over 7 days had no detectable effect on synapse morphology. Both acute and repeated 17β-estradiol exposure were associated with differential expression of oestrogen-related pathways. Together, these data indicate that human cerebral organoids express oestrogen receptors and respond to 17β-estradiol with exposure-dependent changes in synaptic structure accompanied by subtle transcriptional changes.

title: Urinary extracellular vesicle microRNA profile in dogs with visceral leishmaniasis: differential expression and exploratory associations with renal Doppler indices and proteinuria.
abstract: Canine visceral leishmaniasis (CVL) is a systemic zoonosis caused by Leishmania infantum, for which dogs are the main urban reservoir. Infected dogs may present non-specific clinical signs and, in advanced cases, die of chronic kidney disease. This study evaluated urinary microRNAs (miRNAs) as candidate biomarkers of renal injury in naturally infected dogs. Fifteen dogs were included: five healthy controls and ten untreated dogs at the moderate stage of disease according to the LeishVet guidelines. All dogs underwent clinical and laboratory assessment, renal Doppler ultrasonography, and serological and molecular diagnosis of CVL. The CVL group showed typical clinical signs, including onychogryphosis, lymphadenomegaly, and cutaneous lesions, as well as laboratory abnormalities such as hyperglobulinemia. Ultrasonography revealed increased renal echogenicity and an elevated peak systolic velocity in the left kidney. Urinary extracellular vesicles were isolated for RNA extraction and miRNA sequencing (RNA-Seq), followed by bioinformatic analysis. Twenty-one differentially expressed miRNAs were identified, including three with previously described physiological renal expression: miR-486 and miR-378 (up-regulated) and cfa-let-7f (down-regulated). The differentially expressed miRNAs were correlated with renal Doppler indices and the urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio (UPC). Pearson correlation analyses were performed in the infected group, without correction for multiple comparisons. These exploratory analyses identified six statistically significant associations involving five miRNAs: miR-222 was negatively correlated with the resistive index (RI) of both kidneys; miR-95 was negatively correlated with the RI of the left kidney; miR-221 was negatively correlated with the RI of the right kidney; cfa-let-7a-2 was positively correlated with the RI of the left kidney; and cfa-let-7g was negatively correlated with UPC. These findings suggest that the altered urinary miRNA profile may reflect molecular processes associated with renal alterations in dogs with CVL. Urinary miRNAs may therefore be promising candidates for further investigation as minimally invasive biomarkers of renal involvement in canine visceral leishmaniasis.

title: Gene set selection for classification with single-cell RNA-seq.
abstract: Marker genes are important for analyzing and interpreting single-cell RNA-seq (scRNAseq) experiments. They are used to identify and categorize cell types and can also be useful for the design of downstream experiments. We present CellSieve, which tackles the problem of finding effective gene sets rather than distilling markers one at a time. While several "combinatorial" approaches to gene set selection have been proposed, we find that our approach, which leverages a combination of multinomial logistic regression and linear programming, is much more effective at finding small gene sets that can classify cell types.

title: TJP2 inhibits clear cell renal cell carcinoma progression by up-regulating TIMM21 to modulate the SPRY4-ERK1/2 signaling pathway.
abstract: Currently, numerous studies have clearly established the tumor-suppressive role of Tight Junction Protein 2 (TJP2). Although our previous research confirmed the down-regulation of TJP2 in ccRCC, its biological functions and underlying regulatory mechanisms remain poorly understood. In this study, we characterized the biological functions of TJP2 using cell phenotypic assays and mouse orthotopic renal tumor growth model. Subsequently, we identified mitochondrial import inner membrane translocase subunit Tim21 (TIMM21) as the downstream target protein of TJP2 through TMT (Tandem Mass Tags)-based proteomic profiling and co-immunoprecipitation (co-IP) experiment. Furthermore, we elucidated the downstream signaling mechanisms by which the TJP2/TIMM21 axis inhibits ccRCC progression using a combination of IP, Immunofluorescence, Western blotting, qRT-PCR, and RNA-seq analyses. Our experimental results confirmed that TJP2 over-expression significantly inhibits the growth, migration, and invasion of ccRCC cells and promotes cell apoptosis both in vitro and in vivo. TIMM21 is under-expressed in ccRCC, and its decreased expression correlates with unfavorable pathological characteristics and poor patient prognosis. Mechanistically, TJP2 directly binds to TIMM21 protein, promoting its expression and inhibiting its ubiquitination levels. TJP2 over-expression up-regulates SPRY4 expression and inhibits the ERK1/2 signaling pathway. Notably, knockdown of TIMM21 in TJP2-overexpressing cells significantly reverses TJP2-induced cellular phenotypic inhibition, while suppressing SPRY4 expression and promoting pERK1/2 expression. Consistently, knockdown of SPRY4 similarly rescues the inhibited cellular phenotypes caused by TIMM21 over-expression and restores pERK1/2 levels. Our study demonstrates the mechanism by which the TJP2/TIMM21 axis accelerates SPRY4 expression and restrains the ERK1/2 signaling pathway, thereby suppressing ccRCC progression.

title: Single-Cell Sequencing Combined with Genome-Wide Association Studies Reveals Smoking-Associated Key Genes and Putative Downstream Injury Mechanisms in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease.
abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is characterized by persistent airflow obstruction. Cigarette smoking remains a major risk factor. In this study, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) with genome-wide association studies (GWAS) to identify smoking-associated genes that are associated with the pathogenesis of COPD and to computationally infer the downstream injury mechanisms through which they act. Data on COPD and smoking were obtained from public databases. Distinct cell types in COPD were identified through single-cell analysis. Next, pivotal cell populations and candidate genes were delineated by leveraging GWAS analyses linked to single-cell phenotypic characteristics, and candidate genes were identified based on expression level analysis. The biological mechanisms underlying smoking and COPD were examined using functional enrichment and immune infiltration analyses. Four candidate key COPD genes were identified, including SLC34A2, SDC4, DHCR24, and MGST1, which were significantly downregulated in COPD samples. Single-cell RNA-seq analysis revealed that epithelial cells represent an important cell type in COPD, with the key genes being dynamically expressed during epithelial cell differentiation. Seven specific transcription factors were identified in epithelial cells, including RFX3, TEAD1, IRF8, SPI1, IRF8_extended, BHLHE41, and ERG. The four key genes were significantly enriched in the "Protein degradation" pathway and the KEAP1-NFE2L2 oxidative stress pathway. In addition, 23 different immune cell types were identified, and activated B cells were negatively associated with DHCR24, SDC4, and MGST1 expression. Through computational integration, we identified SLC34A2, SDC4, DHCR24, and MGST1 as candidate key genes whose expression in airway epithelial cells is associated with smoking and COPD. Computational analyses suggest that these genes are involved in mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative stress. These results provide a hypothesis-generating basis for future functional studies and for examining these genes as potential biomarkers, although they do not reveal therapeutic targets.
extra: Int J Chron Obstruct Pulmon Dis

title: Dual-platform interleukin profiling reveals a diagnostic cytokine signature and high-risk haplotype in Iraqi bladder cancer.
abstract: Chronic inflammation alters the tumor microenvironment and is the primary cause of bladder cancer (BC), a primary urological cancer. The objective of this study was to analyze the transcriptomic and proteomic expressions of six interleukins (IL-1β, IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, IL-17 A, and IL-23) in Iraqi patients with BC. The study was a prospective case-control study of 266 patients with histologically confirmed BC and 360 age-and sex-matched healthy control individuals. Total RNA was extracted from peripheral blood, reverse-transcribed to cDNA, and interleukin mRNA transcripts were quantified by RT-qPCR, and their protein concentrations were measured using high sensitivity ELISAs. Six functional interleukin-gene polymorphisms were genotyped by TaqMan allelic discrimination for haplotype analysis. The transcriptional and translational levels of the selected six interleukins were significantly elevated. The IL-8 mRNA transcription levels were 12.17 ± 3.48 and had the highest diagnostic metric (AUC = 0.947). The diagnostic metric for IL-17 A was an AUC of 0. 931.The six-IL composite panel had an apparent (in-sample) AUC of 0.978 (optimism-corrected AUC after bootstrap internal validation = 0.964); this estimate requires confirmation in an independent cohort. The level of expression of the six interleukins was significantly elevated with the increase in the tumor grade and the muscle invasion. A strong and direct correlation was achieved with IL-8 serum protein and IL-17 A mRNA measured using the ELISA and RT-qPCR. The cohort of BC patients in Iraq had a multi-interleukin inflammatory signature that identified inflammation with malignancy, was associated with impairment in health, increased with the aggressiveness of the disease, and was influenced by genetic factors with a range of proinflammatory predisposition. The diagnostic performance of the combined panel is an internally validated, in-sample estimate that requires external validation before clinical use.

title: Identification of calcium signaling-associated biomarkers in postmenopausal osteoporosis via multi-omics analysis and experimental validation.
abstract: Calcium signaling dysregulation is a core pathological process in postmenopausal osteoporosis (PMOP). However, no study has systematically explored calcium-related genes as biomarkers in PMOP. Calcium-related genes were intersected from HGNC and GeneCards. The merged dataset of GSE56815 and GSE2208 was used as the discovery set, and GSE56116 and GSE230665 were used as the validation sets. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis and differential expression analysis identified candidate genes. Mendelian randomization (MR) and colocalization were used to identify genetically supported causal genes. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) profiled the bone microenvironment. Receiver Operating Characteristic curves were used to build diagnostic models. Deep learning-based DrugReflector and molecular docking prioritized drugs. Phenome-wide association study (PheWAS) assessed safety. MC3T3-E1 cells under estrogen deprivation were used for in vitro validation. Four PMOP-related calcium genes were identified. MR (OR > 1) and colocalization (conditional PP.H4 = 0.887) supported CAMLG as a causal risk gene for PMOP. scRNA-seq revealed that CAMLG exhibited cell-type specificity, and virtual knockout suggested its involvement in the bone metabolic progression of PMOP. CAMLG had exploratory diagnostic performance (AUCs: 0.735 in the discovery set, 0.967 in blood validation, and 0.889 in femoral validation). Deep learning prioritized BRD-K28178212, which bound CAMLG with - 6.694 kcal/mol. PheWAS showed no significant off-target associations. In estrogen-deprived MC3T3-E1 cells, CAMLG mRNA and protein were upregulated. CAMLG is associated with the promotion of PMOP and may serve as a therapeutic target and diagnostic biomarker for PMOP. BRD-K28178212 was identified as a potential candidate targeted lead compound.

title: Upregulation of KIF18A is associated with poor prognosis and immune alterations in kidney renal papillary cell carcinoma.
abstract: Kidney renal papillary cell carcinoma (KIRP) is a heterogeneous subtype of renal cell carcinoma. Patients with KIRP show variable clinical outcomes. KIF18A is a kinesin-8 motor protein that participates in mitotic chromosome alignment. Previous studies have linked KIF18A to tumor progression. However, its clinical significance and immune relevance in KIRP remain unclear. RNA-sequencing data and clinicopathological information were obtained from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA). Genotype-Tissue Expression (GTEx) samples were incorporated as additional normal controls when appropriate. We analyzed KIF18A expression, diagnostic performance, survival outcomes, clinicopathological associations, immune infiltration, immune-related genes, differentially expressed genes, and pathway enrichment. KIF18A expression was significantly higher in KIRP tumor tissues than in normal kidney tissues. Receiver operating characteristic analysis showed moderate diagnostic performance, with an AUC of 0.693. High KIF18A expression was associated with shorter overall survival, disease-specific survival, and progression-free interval. It was also related to advanced pathological stage, higher T classification, lymph node involvement, and distant metastasis. Immune infiltration analysis showed that high KIF18A expression was positively associated with T helper cells, Th2 cells, central memory T cells, and activated dendritic cells. In contrast, it was negatively associated with CD8 T cells and cytotoxic cells. Several immune-related genes, including CD200, CD40, CD276, IDO1, ICOS, and PDCD1, were upregulated in the high-KIF18A group. Differential expression analysis identified 1,149 genes, including 896 upregulated genes and 253 downregulated genes. These genes were mainly enriched in cell-cycle regulation, chromosome segregation, mitotic spindle organization, epithelial-mesenchymal transition, and metabolism-related processes. KIF18A is upregulated in KIRP and is associated with poor prognosis, aggressive clinicopathological features, and immune-related alterations. These findings suggest that KIF18A may have prognostic and immune-related relevance in KIRP. Further experimental studies and independent clinical validation are required.

title: Revealing the platelet transcriptome using Siphon-seq: a sensitive, purity-aware method for RNA-sequencing.
abstract: Platelet transcriptomics is limited by the exceptionally low RNA content of platelets and by disproportionate contributions from contaminating cells to bulk RNA-sequencing libraries. We developed Siphon-seq, an approach that deliberately overloads independently barcoded single-cell partitions to increase aggregate platelet RNA input, then computationally identifies and removes partitions containing contaminating RNA after sequencing. Applied to 34 healthy human donors, Siphon-seq increased platelet-marker representation, depleted leukocyte and erythrocyte transcripts, and removed contamination-associated inter-donor transcriptional structure. We defined a 3,436-gene core platelet transcriptome that was strongly related to megakaryocyte expression. However, megakaryocyte transcription did not fully explain the platelet transcriptome, which had specific pathways systematically enriched or depleted that were obscured by leukocyte contamination. These findings were confirmed in an independent cohort and were associated with protein detection in two platelet proteome resources. In a pilot human sepsis cohort, Siphon-seq reduced transcripts associated with leukocytes to reveal increased platelet-associated pathway signals. These contaminating immune pathways were also enriched in samples analyzed by bulk RNA-seq from an independent sepsis cohort, most strongly in the stratum with the highest estimated leukocyte burden. Combined, these results reveal that RNA-level contamination can alter both transcriptome structure and biological inference, and that Siphon-seq bridges the sensitivity-purity tradeoff that has limited platelet RNA sequencing, enabling sensitive, purity-aware studies of platelet biology in health and disease.

title: Functional characterization of ALMS1-IT1 in colorectal cancer following TRPM4-correlated lncRNA screening.
abstract: The long non-coding RNA (lncRNA) ALMS1-IT1 has been implicated in colorectal cancer (CRC), but its relationship with cPLA2/PTGS2 expression remains unclear. Transcriptomic and clinical data from 620 patients in TCGA-COAD and TCGA-READ were analyzed; somatic mutation analyses included patients with available mutation data. TRPM4-correlated lncRNAs were screened, and an exploratory prognostic score was developed using Cox and LASSO regression and evaluated using an internal training-validation split. Pathway, immune, mutational, and predicted drug-response features associated with the score were examined. The effects of ALMS1-IT1 knockdown were assessed in CRC cells, and a subcutaneous xenograft assay was performed using siRNA-transfected SW480 cells. The five-lncRNA score comprised AC074212.1, ALMS1-IT1, RBM26-AS1, AC009133.1, and AC147067.1. Patients in the high-risk group had poorer overall survival in both the training and internal validation cohorts. The time-dependent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AU-ROC) was 0.689, 0.667, and 0.623 at 1, 3, and 5 years, respectively. ALMS1-IT1 expression was higher in SW480 and RKO cells than in NCM460 cells. Knockdown reduced EdU incorporation and colony formation, delayed wound closure, and decreased Transwell migration and invasion. These changes were accompanied by reduced PLA2G4A and PTGS2 transcript levels and lower cPLA2 and PTGS2 protein abundance. At the 2-week endpoint, xenograft tumors in the si-ALMS1-IT1 group weighed less than control tumors. TRPM4-correlated screening identified a five-lncRNA score associated with CRC survival and supported functional investigation of ALMS1-IT1. The findings support further investigation of ALMS1-IT1-associated phenotypes and cPLA2/PTGS2 expression changes in CRC. The prognostic score requires external validation, and the mechanisms underlying these observations remain to be determined.

title: scRNAseq of thyroid eye disease orbital fat demonstrates fibroblast thyroid hormone signalling and SPARC production.
abstract: Thyroid eye disease (TED) is a debilitating extrathyroidal manifestation of Graves' disease in which orbital inflammation, extracellular matrix overproduction, and adipose tissue expansion cause proptosis, disfigurement, and sight loss. There remains an unmet need for reliable serum biomarkers of active disease to enable earlier diagnosis and inform treatment decisions. We used single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNAseq) of orbital fat to characterise the pathological landscape of TED, then investigated candidate secreted mediators as circulating biomarkers across multiple independent clinical cohorts. Orbital fat obtained from decompressions in four people with TED was profiled by scRNAseq. In three separate cohorts, serum levels of SPARC, fibronectin, IGF-1, and other serum proteins were measured by ELISA in healthy controls and participants with thyroid disease stratified by TED severity and validated in an independent cohort. Correlations with thyroid function tests (FT3, FT4, and TSH) and longitudinal changes over 48 weeks were also assessed. In additional orbital fat samples, SPARC protein distribution was characterised by immunofluorescence. scRNAseq identified orbital fibroblast subsets expressing thyroid hormone receptors (THRA, THRB), the T4/T3 transporter SLC16A2, DIO2, IGF1R, and extracellular matrix proteins including SPARC. Serum SPARC was significantly elevated in people with thyroid disease compared to healthy controls and was highest in those with moderate-to-sight-threatening TED across all three primary cohorts, with validation in an additional cohort. In moderate-to-sight-threatening TED, serum SPARC correlated positively with FT3 and negatively with TSH. SPARC and IGF-1 were positively correlated regardless of TED status. Longitudinal follow-up demonstrated that serum SPARC declined significantly by week 48 as clinical activity scores fell. Immunofluorescence confirmed heterogeneous SPARC expression by fibroblasts in both control and TED orbital fat. SPARC is highly expressed by orbital fat fibroblasts, its serum levels are elevated in active TED and correlate with both disease severity and thyroid hormone status. These findings suggest SPARC as a promising biomarker of active TED and provide evidence linking circulating T3 to orbital fibrotic processes, further supporting strict thyroid function control in TED management.

title: Multi-cohort and single-cell multi-omic analyses reveal multicellular mechanotransduction-immune remodeling in rheumatoid arthritis synovium.
abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) synovitis integrates immune-cell recruitment, stromal remodeling and persistent inflammation, but its relationship with tissue mechanotransduction remains unclear. We investigated whether RA involves coordinated remodeling of multicellular mechanotransduction-immune programs. We constructed a 327-gene mechanotransduction compendium and used GSE89408 synovial transcriptomes from healthy controls (n = 28), patients with osteoarthritis (n = 22) and patients with RA (n = 152) for discovery. Candidates prioritized through RA-versus-Healthy and RA-versus-OA contrasts were evaluated in three patient-independent cohorts using validation-only random-effects meta-analysis. Co-expression networks, consensus clustering, locked external mapping, single-cell RNA sequencing, cell-cell communication inference, virtual knockout and single-cell chromatin-accessibility analyses (11 RA donors and one OA reference; no healthy controls) resolved network, cellular and regulatory contexts. Selected gene-expression findings were examined by quantitative PCR in independent healthy (n = 20) and RA (n = 25) synovial tissues and by overexpression and siRNA-mediated knockdown in synovial fibroblasts. In unadjusted bulk-tissue profiles, RA synovium showed higher expression-based scores for integrin-extracellular matrix sensing and nuclear LINC programs but lower scores for focal-adhesion force-transmission and Hippo-YAP/TAZ-associated genes. Composition adjustment attenuated several of these associations. Nine candidates met the prespecified meta-analysis criteria and mapped to four co-expression modules associated with adaptive and innate immune programs, cell cycling and mechanotransduction-related expression scores. Tissue qPCR reproduced the predicted expression directions. Two molecular states with distinct inflammatory and mechanotransduction-associated expression features were recovered in external cohorts. In exploratory analyses, TLN2 and NRXN1 expression was inversely associated with inflammatory mediators and DAS28. Exploratory single-cell analyses localized the programs to fibroblast, myeloid, lymphoid and proliferating states and inferred differences in fibroblast-myeloid communication potential. Perturbing TLN2 or NRXN1 altered selected ECM-associated transcripts and COL1A1 protein, with corresponding changes in Matrigel invasion within one donor, while transcription-factor perturbation supported candidate FOXP2-NRXN1, NFIX-NRXN1/TLN2 and FOS-TLN2 expression relationships. Patient-derived multi-omic and experimental evidence supports coordinated transcriptional remodeling of a multicellular mechanotransduction-immune network associated with RA synovial heterogeneity.

title: Integrated multi-omics analysis identifies ELF1 as a B-Cell-associated prognostic biomarker in breast cancer.
abstract: Breast cancer progression is influenced not only by tumor-intrinsic alterations but also by interactions within the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME). We aimed to identify genetically regulated susceptibility genes associated with immune-related cellular states in breast cancer. We first performed a transcriptome-wide association study (TWAS) using FinnGen summary statistics to identify candidate genetically regulated genes associated with breast cancer susceptibility. Their transcriptional activity was subsequently mapped onto the GSE176078 single-cell atlas using AUCell, UCell, and AddModuleScore. Because B cells consistently showed the highest enrichment, we further applied hdWGCNA to characterize co-expression modules associated with the high TWAS score (HTS) state. We then integrated LASSO, Random Forest, Boruta, and XGBoost analyses to prioritize candidate hub genes. The prognostic and immunological relevance of ELF1 was further evaluated in GSE96058 (n = 3,273) and METABRIC (n = 2,509). Functional validation was further performed using ELF1-modulated B-cell models, including Raji and GM12878 cells, together with direct co-culture assays with MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cells. TWAS analysis identified 65 candidate genetically regulated genes, and their activity appeared to be preferentially enriched in B cells. hdWGCNA further linked HTS-associated modules to RNA splicing and B-cell activation pathways. Among the candidate genes, ELF1 was the only candidate feature consistently prioritized across all four machine learning algorithms. Low ELF1 expression was associated with inferior overall survival in the GSE96058 cohort, while a consistent survival trend was observed in the METABRIC cohort. ELF1 expression positively correlated with naive B-cell infiltration but showed negative correlations with plasma cells and M0/M1 macrophages. Functional experiments demonstrated that ELF1 modulation affected B-cell proliferation, activation marker expression, RNA splicing-related molecules, and altered the proliferative and invasive behaviors of breast cancer cells in direct co-culture systems. By integrating TWAS, single-cell transcriptomics, machine learning, and preliminary experimental validation, we identified ELF1 as a B-cell-associated prognostic biomarker in breast cancer. These findings suggest that ELF1 may represent a molecular link between genetically regulated expression patterns and B-cell-related immune states within the tumor microenvironment.

title: An integrative network toxicology and single-cell analysis implicates a potential myeloid-centered plaque remodeling axis in bisphenol A-related atherosclerosis.
abstract: Bisphenol A (BPA) is a widely exposed endocrine-disrupting chemical that has been associated with multiple cardiovascular abnormalities, yet its cell-type-specific molecular mechanisms and potential effects within the atherosclerotic plaque microenvironment remain unclear. This study aimed to systematically identify BPA-related molecular networks in atherosclerosis (AS) and characterize their potential roles within the plaque microenvironment through integrated network toxicology, machine learning, molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and single-cell transcriptomics. GSE43292 and GSE100927 were integrated as the discovery cohort for differential expression analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) to identify AS-related key genes. BPA targets predicted using ChEMBL, SwissTargetPrediction, and the Similarity Ensemble Approach (SEA) were intersected with AS key genes to obtain BPA-AS candidate targets. An ensemble of 127 machine-learning model combinations was developed using the discovery cohort, while GSE28829, GSE40231, and GSE163154 were used as external cohorts for out-of-cohort model evaluation and comparison. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), Cell-type Identification By Estimating Relative Subsets Of RNA Transcripts (CIBERSORT), molecular docking, MD simulations, and the single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) dataset GSE159677 were further applied to interpret model performance, characterize immune infiltration, assess predicted BPA-protein interactions, and investigate plaque microenvironmental mechanisms using CellChat, scTenifoldKnk, and MultiNicheNet. A total of 29 BPA-AS candidate targets were identified, mainly enriched in innate immune activation, lysosomal function, and lipid-and-atherosclerosis-related pathways. The random forest model identified 13 hub genes with good discriminatory performance, and SHAP analysis highlighted KCND3, RNASE1, HEXIM1, and TNF as major contributors to model prediction. Immune infiltration analysis revealed increased myeloid components, particularly Macrophages M0, in AS, with significant correlations with multiple hub genes. Molecular docking suggested favorable structural compatibility between BPA and several hub-gene-encoded proteins, while 100-ns MD simulations of the BPA-PLA2G15, BPA-TNF, and BPA-RNASE1 complexes provided complementary dynamic support for persistent BPA association with the predicted binding-pocket regions, despite different degrees of ligand rearrangement. Single-cell analysis further demonstrated marked myeloid enrichment in calcified atherosclerotic core (AC) samples and cell-type-specific distribution of the hub genes. CellChat identified an enhanced TNF-TNFRSF1B signaling axis in AC, while scTenifoldKnk and MultiNicheNet supported myeloid-centered inflammatory and vascular/stromal remodeling programs. Collectively, these findings suggest that predicted BPA-related targets may intersect with AS-associated inflammatory activation, lysosomal lipid metabolism, vascular remodeling, and myeloid-centered communication programs. This study provides a multilayer, hypothesis-generating framework for investigating potential molecular links between BPA and AS.

title: Mono(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate may promote lung adenocarcinoma stromal remodeling through ADARB1-dependent fibroblast activation: Integrated bioinformatic, biophysical and cellular evidence.
abstract: Di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP) is a widely used plasticizer, and its bioactive metabolite mono(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (MEHP) is ubiquitously detected in environmental and biological matrices. This study aimed to characterize the molecular events linking MEHP exposure to stromal remodeling in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). LUAD candidate targets were identified by integrating differential expression analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) across multiple GEO transcriptomic datasets. MEHP targets retrieved from ChEMBL, CTD and SwissTargetPrediction were intersected with LUAD candidate targets, followed by functional enrichment analysis and machine learning-based core gene prioritization. The cellular localization and functional context of the core target ADARB1 were delineated via single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis. Direct interaction between MEHP and ADARB1 was validated by surface plasmon resonance (SPR) assay. Expression regulation and functional mediation of ADARB1 were further verified in primary human pulmonary microvascular endothelial cells (PMECs) and human lung fibroblasts (HLFs). ADARB1 was the only candidate gene consistently selected by LASSO regression, random forest and SVM-RFE algorithms. Bulk transcriptomic analysis showed downregulated ADARB1 expression in LUAD tissues, whereas scRNA-seq revealed specific enrichment of ADARB1 in endothelial cells and fibroblasts. High ADARB1 expression in stromal cells was associated with endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EndMT)-like trajectories, TGF-β/NF-κB/HIF-1/integrin signaling, and extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling. SPR assay confirmed direct binding between MEHP and ADARB1 with an equilibrium dissociation constant (Kd) of 11.19 μM. In vitro, MEHP concentration-dependently upregulated ADARB1 at both mRNA and protein levels in PMECs and HLFs, with higher sensitivity observed in HLFs. Knockdown of ADARB1 significantly attenuated MEHP-induced upregulation of fibroblast activation markers (α-SMA, FAP) and ECM proteins (FN1, COL1A1) in HLFs. These findings suggest that MEHP may drive LUAD stromal remodeling by activating fibroblasts via an ADARB1-dependent mechanism, providing testable mechanistic hypotheses and candidate biomarkers for phthalate-associated cancer risk assessment.

title: Urinary 2-hydroxynaphthalene is associated with late-life poor cognitive performance and ADRM1-related microglial state alterations.
abstract: Environmental exposures are modifiable dementia-related risks, but population biomonitoring signals are rarely linked to Alzheimer's disease (AD) biology. In 579 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2011 to 2014 adults aged ≥60 years, poor cognitive performance (PCP) was defined using Consortium to Establish a Registry for Alzheimer's Disease Animal Fluency and Digit Symbol Substitution scores. Environmental biomarkers were prioritized using complementary machine-learning methods; epidemiologic inference used survey-weighted regression and restricted cubic splines. AD-relevant contextualization included an exploratory amyloid positron emission tomography-positive AD cohort, network toxicology, docking, human-brain single-cell transcriptomics, and lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-primed BV-2 assays incorporating protein, cytokine, amyloid beta engagement assays, and a tiered transcriptional strategy composed of targeted reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction and bulk RNA sequencing. Urinary 2-hydroxynaphthalene (2-HN) was the only environmental analyte retained across models, showed an upper-range non-linear association with PCP, and persisted after urinary-creatinine adjustment (p for overall = 0.003; p for non-linearity < 0.001). Mechanistic analyses converged on proteasome/AD pathways, and the docking-prioritized candidate-gene score localized to gliovascular cells and showed a modest, exploratory association with apolipoprotein E (APOE)/triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 2 (TREM2)-associated microglial features. In LPS-primed BV-2 cells, 2-HN reduced adhesion regulating molecule 1 (ADRM1) protein at 1 µM, and Adrm1 transcript abundance at 1 and 10 µM. Apoe was markedly increased at both concentrations, whereas Trem2 increased significantly only at 10 µM. RNA sequencing indicated remodeling of immune-signaling pathways. Urinary 2-HN is a candidate combustion-related biomarker associated with cognitive vulnerability and implicates ADRM1-related microglial proteostasis alterations and state transitions.

title: Multimodal Single-Cell Analysis Reveals the Prognostic Role of Myeloid Subpopulation-Associated PI3K/AKT Signaling in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) represents a major global health burden with rising incidence, marked heterogeneity, and poor prognosis, necessitating reliable biomarkers for prognostic stratification. This study conducted a comprehensive multi-omics analysis, combining a large amount of RNA-seq data from TCGA-LIHC with a single-cell RNA-seq database. Feature extraction using autoencoders and 12 machine learning algorithms was applied to identify prognostic biomarkers, followed by survival analysis, single-cell atlas construction, and experimental validation. Using multi-gene representations from autoencoders, the authors determined that the PI3K/AKT pathway is a critical survival-related pathway. Integrated single-cell analysis uncovered 12 distinct cellular clusters, with the myeloid subpopulation showing pronounced transcriptional dysregulation driven by PI3K/AKT signaling. The intersection of 2,567 upregulated genes from myeloid cells and 105 PI3K/AKT pathway-related genes identified 24 overlapping candidates. LASSO optimization yielded a robust predictive model (ROC-AUC = 0.949), consistently identifying RAC1 and SLC2A1 as core prognostic genes validated in the external cohort GSE76427. Both genes showed strong associations with adverse survival outcomes and EMT pathway activation. Western blot experiments confirmed that RAC1 and SLC2A1 knockdown modulate PI3K/AKT pathway activity, while transwell assays demonstrated suppressed migration and invasion. This study establishes a comprehensive framework integrating multi-omics profiling, single-cell transcriptomics, and machine learning to dissect HCC molecular heterogeneity. This study identified the PI3K/AKT signaling axis as a key prognostic driver in tumor-associated bone marrow subgroups and identified candidate biomarkers RAC1 and SLC2A1, providing mechanistic insights for the development of targeted therapies for this challenging malignant tumor.

title: Multi-omics analysis identified ASRGL1 as a novel oncogene and potential therapeutic target in prostate cancer.
abstract: Prostate Cancer (PCa) is a globally prevalent malignancy with high heterogeneity and frequent therapy resistance. Identifying novel causal drivers and understanding their roles in the tumor microenvironment (TME) are crucial for developing new therapeutic strategies. We employed an integrative multi-omics approach. First, we analyzed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data from prostate tissues to identify differentially expressed genes. Mendelian Randomization (MR) analysis was then performed using cis-expression quantitative trait loci (cis-eQTLs) and cis-protein QTLs (cis-pQTLs) from the deCODE database to infer causal relationships between gene/protein expression and PCa risk. Findings were validated using bulk transcriptomic and clinical data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) cohort. Functional enrichment, immune microenvironment analysis, and drug sensitivity profiling were conducted to elucidate the oncogenic mechanisms of the candidate gene. MR analysis identified asparaginase-like 1 (ASRGL1) as a novel causal risk factor for PCa (OR = 1.074, 95% CI: 1.032-1.118, P < 0.001). Consistently, ASRGL1 expression was significantly upregulated in PCa tumors and associated with poor patient prognosis. scRNA-seq analysis revealed that ASRGL1 was predominantly expressed in mast cells within the TME. Functional studies indicated that high ASRGL1 expression correlated with activated cell cycle pathways, dysregulated cholesterol homeostasis, and an immunosuppressive TME. Furthermore, we identified several potential therapeutic compounds (e.g., panobinostat, pevonedistat) that showed predicted efficacy against ASRGL1-high PCa models. Our study establishes ASRGL1 as a causal oncogene in PCa, linking its expression to mast cell function, metabolic reprogramming, and immune suppression. These findings nominate ASRGL1 as a promising prognostic biomarker and a potential therapeutic target, offering new insights for PCa treatment.
